caption: Each layer adds its header, so 1,460 bytes of data go down the stack and leave as a 1,518-byte frame: 58 bytes of overhead, 96.2% user data. Those same 58 bytes make a 10-byte message only 14.7% efficient.

spec.aria: A five-step stack shows a 1,460-byte message grow to a 1,480-byte segment with a 20-byte TCP header, a 1,500-byte packet with a 20-byte IP header, and a 1,518-byte frame with a 14-byte header plus 4-byte trailer, then bits on the medium, with the frame stage highlighted.
